accuracy_findings.claim: Population is the number of inhabitants of a system, counted in points.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1204-1213 population is a Core.DynamicValue float; workforce = floor(population.value). Counted in points, matches style rule 3.4.9.

accuracy_findings.claim: A system starts at {const:system_starting_population} population when it is colonized (Legacy 15.8).
accuracy_findings.evidence: colonization.ex:37 allows only :uninhabited targets -> claim/4 stellar_system.ex:251-254 calls open_system for :uninhabitable/:uninhabited -> :1420 population = DynamicValue.new(c.system_starting_population). Run of population-acc-r0-growth.exs: slow start_pop=15.8, medium 15.8, fast 5.0; the compiled fast page reads 'starts at 5 population', medium 15.8.

accuracy_findings.claim: a neutral system starts there when the galaxy is created.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:186-189: status == :inhabited_neutral -> open_system(state), which sets the starting population (:1420).

accuracy_findings.claim: Only whole points count. The system's workforce is its population rounded down
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1213 workforce: floor(population.value); collect_initial_bonuses :1827-1832 multiplies by state.workforce. Script: floor(15.8)=15. Population is never negative (:1265-1266), so rounding down is the same as truncation. Population class (:1537) reads the raw population.value, but its thresholds are whole numbers and it is only recomputed when the workforce changes (:1215-1219), so the sentence holds in practice.

accuracy_findings.claim: each of those points pays [[taxes]]: {const:system_population_taxes_factor} credits per day (Legacy 2)
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1831 base_taxes = c.system_population_taxes_factor * state.workforce, added at :1853-1856 as :add to :sys_credit. Script: taxes=2 at all three speeds. The UI shows a time unit as a day (game.json 'day': '{n}d').

accuracy_findings.claim: plus the [[mobility]] bonus
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1832 base_mobility = c.system_mobility_taxes_factor * workforce, applied as :mul from :sys_mobility to :sys_credit (:1857-1860). Script: mob=0.1.

accuracy_findings.claim: changes [[stability]] by {const:system_population_negative_happiness_factor} (renders -1)
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1830 base_population = c.system_population_negative_happiness_factor * workforce, added at :1849-1852 to :sys_happiness. Script: neg_happy=-1.0 at every speed.

accuracy_findings.claim: adds {const:system_base_defense} defense in a system you own (Legacy 0.15)
accuracy_findings.evidence: Legacy and Tactic are correct: stellar_system.ex:1825-1828 adds system_base_defense * workforce only when status == :inhabited_player (script: slow 0.15, medium 0.15). At Flash, constant-fast.ex:10 has system_base_defense: 0.0. The compiled fast page reads 'adds 0 defense in a system you own. Dominions and neutral systems get no defense from population.', which implies owned systems do get defense from population when they get none at that speed.
accuracy_findings.fix: Word it so a zero value still reads correctly, e.g. 'adds {const:system_base_defense} defense, only in a system you own (none at speeds where this is 0)'. Or move the defense line into a sentence that does not contrast owned systems with dominions. The writer must check the fast render.

accuracy_findings.claim: Dominions and neutral systems get no defense from population.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1825-1828: base_defense is 0 unless status == :inhabited_player. Consistent with confirmed quirk 8.1 ('Population defends'); not contradicted.

accuracy_findings.claim: Population changes every day by the growth below
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:881-886 next_tick -> update_population(elapsed_time); :1263 new_population = population + growth * elapsed_time, a per-time-unit rate. Ticks are scheduled every 2 units while change != 0 (:194-197), which the per-day wording is consistent with.

accuracy_findings.claim: and never drops below 0.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1265-1266: new_population < 0 -> {0, 0}. Script: next(h0, p0.001, s-20, et2) = {0, 0}. The stored growth also becomes 0 in that case.

clarity_findings.problem: The prose states the housing factor "turns negative once population passes housing + 0.75" but never says what that does. The formula multiplies this factor into growth, so a negative housing factor makes growth negative once population is far enough above housing (population actually shrinks back toward housing). This is exactly the kind of edge case rule 8 says must be spelled out in one sentence rather than left for the reader to derive from the formula.
clarity_findings.quote: The housing factor turns negative once population passes housing + 0.75.
clarity_findings.fix: Add one clause stating the consequence, e.g. "...housing + 0.75, at which point growth turns negative and population shrinks back down."

clarity_findings.problem: One run-on sentence tries to both define workforce and introduce the bulleted per-point effects, and the referent of "those points" is ambiguous on first read — it isn't clear whether the effects belong to workforce specifically or to population generally (workforce and "whole points of population" happen to be the same number here, but the sentence doesn't say so plainly).
clarity_findings.quote: Only whole points count. The system's [[workforce]] is its population rounded down, and each of those points:
clarity_findings.fix: Split into two sentences, e.g. "Only whole points count, so the system's [[workforce]] is its population rounded down. Each whole point of population:"

clarity_findings.problem: "changes [[stability]] by {const:system_population_negative_happiness_factor}" compiles to "changes stability by -1", which forces the reader to do the sign arithmetic themselves to learn stability goes down. Every other bullet states its effect directionally ("pays", "adds"); this one is the odd one out and reads awkwardly.
clarity_findings.fix: State the direction in words, e.g. "lowers [[stability]] by {const:system_population_negative_happiness_factor}" (keeping the token so the sign in the const value can still be checked against the stated direction by lint/reviewers).

clarity_findings.problem: "Dominions" is used with no definition and no link (the dominions page doesn't exist yet), so a first-time reader has no way to know what distinguishes a dominion from a system they own or a neutral system — the sentence only works if you already know the three-way categorization.
clarity_findings.quote: Dominions and neutral systems get no defense from population.
clarity_findings.fix: Not fully fixable until the dominions page exists per the plan, but consider a 3-5 word parenthetical (e.g. "Dominions (systems you don't directly control)") to keep the sentence self-contained until the link is available.

clarity_findings.problem: The UI-behavior sentence about the growth label box is dropped between the growth-formula explanation and the worked example, breaking the formula→example flow that rule 1 asks for; it reads as a tangent inserted mid-derivation rather than either leading into or following the numeric example.
clarity_findings.quote: In the system view, the {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce} box names the growth, from {ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_0} to {ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_5}, and its bar shows progress toward the next whole point.
clarity_findings.fix: Move this sentence either right after "Housing sets the target, stability sets the speed" (before the formula) or after the worked example, so the formula-to-example sequence isn't interrupted.

votes.accuracy_reason: Verified: at Flash the compiled page reads "adds 0 defense in a system you own. Dominions and neutral systems get no defense from population," which reads as owned systems getting the same nothing as dominions/neutrals — misleading even though each clause is literally true; and the housing-factor decline is genuinely unbounded below (stellar_system.ex:1251-1252 caps it only above), so "stability sets the speed" hides that higher stability actually accelerates shrinkage far above housing — a real gap a new player would want to know.
votes.clarity_reason: Several real first-read stumbles confirmed against docs/help-manual.md 3.4: the negative housing factor's consequence (population shrinks back toward housing) is never stated (rule 8), "changes stability by -1" makes the reader do sign arithmetic instead of saying "lowers" like the other bullets, and the workforce/"those points" sentence plus the UI-box aside both disrupt otherwise-clean reading (ambiguous referent, and a tangent breaking the formula-to-example flow rule 1 asks for).

votes.accuracy_reason: Spot-checked the two most serious findings myself: rendering the page at --speed fast (mix help.check --live --page population --speed fast) confirms the defense bullet reads "adds 0 defense in a system you own. Dominions and neutral systems get no defense from population" — a Flash/fast player sees 0 everywhere yet the sentence implies owned systems get something dominions don't, which is a genuine "wrong" (misleading-by-omission) finding per rule 8; and stellar_system.ex:1249-1252 confirms the habitation factor is only capped from above (Enum.min with 1, no lower clamp despite the "[-1,1]" comment), so the missing "no lower limit / faster shrink at higher stability" edge case is a real gap a veteran player would eventually notice as unexplained sudden-collapse behavior. I also confirmed conquest/dominion-conversion leaves population untouched (open_system only fires for :uninhabited/:uninhabitable, stellar_system.ex:251-254), supporting the other missing item. One "wrong" verdict I agree with caps this at 3, and the fast-speed defense line is exactly the kind of number-vs-prose mismatch a player would notice in play, so I'm scoring 2.
votes.clarity_reason: Prose is otherwise clean and follows the say-then-formula-then-example structure (rule 1), but it violates rule 8 by stating "the housing factor turns negative once population passes housing + 0.75" without ever saying what a negative factor does to growth (population shrinks back toward housing), leaves "changes stability by -1" un-directional against the other bullets' active verbs, and drops the UI-behavior sentence about the growth label box awkwardly between the formula and the worked example, breaking the formula→example flow — all real reader friction, but not enough to make the page unusable, so 3 rather than lower.

votes.accuracy_reason: Verified in code: habitation_factor is clamped only from above (Enum.min([...,1]), stellar_system.ex:1251-1252) so the missing-lower-bound finding is real, and system_base_defense is 0.0 at Flash (constant-fast.ex:10) vs 0.15 elsewhere (constant-slow/medium.ex:10), so "adds 0 defense in a system you own. Dominions and neutral systems get no defense from population." reads as a false owned-vs-dominion contrast at Flash speed even though each clause is individually true — I agree this is a misleading/"wrong" finding, which caps the score, and it's compounded by the unbounded-decline omission (a real edge case per rule 8) plus two lower-priority missing items (conquest keeps population, no population-class link).

rebuttals.finding: Code-accuracy critic (missing, optional): 'Conquest keeps the population the system already has.'
rebuttals.evidence: This is only half right, so I applied a narrower wording. claim/4 does not reset population (stellar_system.ex:251-254). But conquest.ex:123-141 sends {:release_siege, lost_population_chances, ...} before claim_system at :154, with 0.02/0.10/0.20/0.05 chances by dice result, and raid/4 (stellar_system.ex:297-315) subtracts population.value * lost_population_chances. A conquered system therefore loses 2-20% of its population, so 'keeps' would be wrong. The page says 'does not reset its population' instead; siege losses belong to the planned siege page.

clarity_findings.problem: First mention of the credits resource lacks the icon+link treatment every sibling page uses. taxes.md writes '{icon:resource/credit} [[credit|credits]]' and credit.md/housing.md/workforce.md follow the same pattern; population.md's bullet gives bare 'credits' with no icon and no [[credit|credits]] link, even though 'credit' is an existing, linkable page.
clarity_findings.quote: pays [[taxes]]: {const:system_population_taxes_factor} credits per day, plus the [[mobility]] bonus;
clarity_findings.fix: Change to: pays [[taxes]]: {const:system_population_taxes_factor} {icon:resource/credit} [[credit|credits]] per day, plus the [[mobility]] bonus;

clarity_findings.problem: [[population-class]] is a bare hyphenated slug. Per compiler.ex:302-304 (default_label), a hyphenated/slashed target with no explicit label falls back to the page's raw title, so this renders mid-sentence as '...the system's Population class.' — an unwanted mid-sentence capital letter (title-cased 'Population', lowercase 'class') that reads as a typo to a player.
clarity_findings.fix: Supply an explicit lowercase label, matching how the page handles [[housing|Housing]] and how stability.md handles [[system-penalties|output penalty]]: Population also sets the system's [[population-class|population class]].

clarity_findings.problem: The Growth section re-derives the full growth model that housing.md already owns and states in the same words: the identical 'housing factor = min((housing + 0.75 − population) × 0.1, 1)' formula, and the same 'population overshoots housing, growth goes negative, population shrinks back' narrative, each with its own separate worked examples. A player reading both pages gets the housing-factor logic twice, and any future formula change has two prose spots to keep in sync instead of one.
clarity_findings.fix: Let housing.md own the housing-factor derivation and its example; population.md's Growth section should state the growth model at a higher level (the stability thresholds and the size factor, which are unique to this page) and link to [[housing]] for how the housing factor itself behaves, rather than restating the formula and re-deriving 'turns negative above housing' in its own words. This also frees up word budget (see word count note).

clarity_findings.problem: This sentence packs two separate comparisons into one clause a first-time reader has to untangle: (1) systems with stability >= 0 vs. systems with negative stability shrink at different relative rates once above housing, and (2) within the stability >= 0 regime, higher stability shrinks faster — which is the opposite of what 'higher stability is better' primes a reader to expect. It needs a second read to parse correctly.
clarity_findings.quote: The housing factor has no lower limit: far above housing, a system with stability 0 or more shrinks faster than one with negative stability, and higher stability makes it shrink faster.
clarity_findings.fix: Split into two sentences, e.g.: 'The housing factor has no lower limit, so a system far above housing keeps shrinking. Above housing, higher stability makes it shrink faster — the opposite of its effect below housing.' The second worked example already shows this numerically (stability 25: −0.183, stability 0: −0.052, stability −5: −0.001); consider pointing to it explicitly instead of stating the relationship abstractly first.

clarity_findings.problem: Resolved through the tokens (game.json: population.workforce = "Population", growth_0..growth_5 = "Very High".."Negative"), this sentence reads to a player as: "In the system view, the Population box names the growth, from Very High to Negative, and its bar shows progress toward the next whole point." 'Names the growth, from X to Y' reads like a continuum between two named endpoints rather than one of six discrete labels, and 'box' is a generic, undefined term (workforce.md calls the same UI element by the same token but describes it more concretely as holding a mobilized/total readout).
clarity_findings.quote: In the system view, the {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce} box names the growth, from {ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_0} to {ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_5}, and its bar shows progress toward the next whole point.
clarity_findings.fix: Reword to name it as a label choice, not a range, e.g.: "In the system view, the {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce} box labels today's growth rate (one of {ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_0} through {ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_5}); its bar fills toward the next whole population point."

clarity_findings.problem: Could not obtain the compiled/rendered text for this page to double-check token resolution and wrapped line length as a player would actually see it. `mix help.check --live --only population --text population` (and even without --text) crashes before producing output: `** (ArgumentError) the Access module supports only keyword lists (with atom keys), got: "3"` at lib/rc/help/format.ex:99 (has_data_key?/2) via compiler.ex:256 (resolve_inline). The crash happens during full-corpus compilation (not scoped by --only) and is unrelated to any token in population.md itself (no {name:} tokens with a numeric key appear in this file) — it looks like a {name:} or {table:}-driven lookup elsewhere in the corpus (e.g. a population-class-style table with a numeric key) tripping RC.Help.Format.has_data_key?/2's use of get_in/2 on a non-keyword path. This blocks compiled-text verification for every page, not just this one, until fixed.
clarity_findings.fix: Not a page-content fix — flagging for the pipeline: RC.Help.Format.has_data_key?/2 (lib/rc/help/format.ex:99) needs to handle non-atom/numeric path segments before calling Access.get/get_in, or the caller needs to stop feeding it a string like "3" as a path segment. Until this is fixed, clarity/accuracy critics can only review source markdown, not the compiled --text view.

accuracy_findings.claim: Population is the number of inhabitants of a system, counted in points.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1208-1213: population is a Core.DynamicValue float and workforce = floor(population.value). There is no 'people' conversion anywhere in the code.

accuracy_findings.claim: A system starts at {const:system_starting_population} population when it is colonized (renders 15.8 at Legacy and medium, 5 at fast)
accuracy_findings.evidence: colonization.ex:91 casts :claim_system, which reaches claim/4 (stellar_system.ex:251-254). For :uninhabitable/:uninhabited systems that calls open_system, which sets population to DynamicValue.new(c.system_starting_population) (:1420). Script population-acc-r2-growth.exs printed start=15.8 (slow), 15.8 (medium), 5.0 (fast), matching all three renders.

accuracy_findings.claim: a neutral system starts there when the galaxy is created
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:185-188: new/… calls open_system(state) when status == :inhabited_neutral, and open_system sets system_starting_population (:1420).

accuracy_findings.claim: Taking an inhabited system, by conquest or as a dominion, does not reset its population.
accuracy_findings.evidence: conquest.ex:154 casts {:claim_system}, and make_dominion.ex:142 casts {:claim_dominion}. Both go through galaxy/agent.ex:82 to StellarSystem.claim/4. There, open_system runs only when status is :uninhabitable/:uninhabited or for a daily initial system (stellar_system.ex:251-254). The only other assignments to population in lib/game are the tick (:1213) and pillage (:315).

accuracy_findings.claim: Population also sets the system's population class.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1533-1541: update_population_class picks the first class whose threshold is <= population.value. It is called from compute_bonus (:1327).

accuracy_findings.claim: Only whole points count, so the system's workforce is its population rounded down.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1213 sets workforce: floor(population.value). collect_initial_bonuses (:1827-1832) multiplies by state.workforce, not by population.

accuracy_findings.claim: Each whole point pays taxes: {const:system_population_taxes_factor} credits per day, plus the mobility bonus
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1831 and :1853-1856 add base_taxes = system_population_taxes_factor * workforce to sys_credit. :1832 and :1857-1860 add a :mul from sys_mobility of system_mobility_taxes_factor * workforce. The script printed taxes=2 and mob=0.1 at every speed. The UI names the rate 'Income / day' (game.json:1597).

accuracy_findings.claim: lowers stability ({const:system_population_negative_happiness_factor} per point) — renders '(-1 per point)'
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1830 and :1849-1852 add system_population_negative_happiness_factor * workforce to sys_happiness. The script printed happ=-1.0 at all speeds.

accuracy_findings.claim: adds {const:system_base_defense} defense, counted only in systems you own directly, never in dominions or neutral systems
accuracy_findings.evidence: Legacy and medium are correct: stellar_system.ex:1825-1828 adds base_defense = system_base_defense * workforce only when status == :inhabited_player, else 0, and the script printed defense=0.15. At fast, constant-fast.ex:10 has system_base_defense: 0.0 (script: fast defense=0.0), and the --page population --speed fast render reads 'adds 0 defense, counted only in systems you own directly…'. That tells a fast-speed player population defends when it adds nothing.
accuracy_findings.fix: Make the bullet speed-safe. For example, keep the {const:} and add a clause that this is 0 on fast, or phrase it as 'adds {const:system_base_defense} defense per point (none on fast)' so the fast render does not describe a zero bonus as a real one. The claim must stay a flat statement (docs 8.1, population defends).

accuracy_findings.claim: Population changes every day by the growth below
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:886 calls update_population(elapsed_time) on every system tick, and :1263 applies new_population = population + growth * elapsed_time. :194-197 schedules a tick every 2 ut while population.change != 0. The UI calls the time unit a day (game.json:1597 'Income / day').

accuracy_findings.claim: and never drops below 0
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1265-1267 returns {0, 0} when new_population < 0. Script: next_tick(h10, p50, s25, elapsed 1000) returned {0, 0}.

accuracy_findings.claim: Housing sets the target, stability sets the speed.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1250-1252: the housing factor is zero at housing + 0.75, so that is the target. :1246-1247 and :1234-1239: stability changes the rate. The size factor (:1257) also scales speed, and the page states that in the formula block.

accuracy_findings.claim: stability < −10: −0.002 per day; −10 ≤ stability < 0: −0.001 per day
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1234-1239 (happiness < -10 -> -0.002; happiness < 0 -> -0.001). Script: h10 p50 s-15 -> growth -0.002, s-5 -> -0.001.

accuracy_findings.claim: stability ≥ 0: (base + min(stability, 25) × 0.002) × housing factor × size factor; base = {const:system_base_growth}; housing factor = min((housing + 0.75 − population) × 0.1, 1); size factor = (1 − min(population, 120) / 120) × 0.8 + 0.2
accuracy_findings.evidence: This matches the verbatim copy of stellar_system.ex:1241-1260 in population-acc-r2-growth.exs. The literals 0.002, 25, 0.75, 0.1, 120, 0.8 and 0.2 are hard-coded, and :1204-1268 is listed in sources. base_growth printed 0.02 (slow), 0.04 (medium) and 0.03 (fast), matching each render.

accuracy_findings.claim: Stability above 25 adds nothing.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1246 (Enum.min([happiness, 25])). Script: h10 p50 at s25 and s40 both returned growth -0.1831666.

accuracy_findings.claim: The size factor falls from 1 at 0 population to 0.2 at 120 population and above.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1257. Script at stability 25 with ample housing: pop 0 -> growth 0.07 (= 0.07 × 1 × 1). Pop 120 and pop 150 both -> 0.014 (= 0.07 × 1 × 0.2).

accuracy_findings.claim: The housing factor turns growth negative once population passes housing + 0.75
The housing factor has no lower limit, so a system far above housing keeps shrinking.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_system.ex:1252 applies only Enum.min([factor, 1]), with no lower clamp. Script: h10 p50 gives housing factor -3.925 and growth -0.183 at s25.

accuracy_findings.claim: There, stability works in reverse: at 0 or more, higher stability makes population shrink faster, and faster than at negative stability.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Script, h10 p50: s25 -0.1832, s0 -0.0523, s-5 -0.001, s-15 -0.002. 'Far above' carries the condition. A boundary scan at stability 0 found the shrink passes -0.001 once population exceeds housing by 1.27 (pop 5), 1.5 (pop 50) or 3.25 (pop 120+). It passes -0.002 once the excess is 1.79, 2.25 or 5.75 at those populations. Just above the threshold it does not hold: h20 p21 gives s0 -0.00043 vs s-5 -0.001. So the sentence is true only because of 'far'.

accuracy_findings.claim: Example (Legacy, housing 30, population 20, stability 15): 0.05 × 1 × 0.867 = +0.043 population per day
accuracy_findings.evidence: Run of a verbatim copy of stellar_system.ex:1226-1268 (tmp/help-review/population-acc-r2-growth.exs): ex1 h30 p20 s15 -> {20.0433, 0.043333}.

accuracy_findings.claim: Example (Legacy, housing 10, population 50): stability 25: 0.07 × −3.925 × 0.667 = −0.183; stability 0: 0.02 × −3.925 × 0.667 = −0.052; stability −5: −0.001
accuracy_findings.evidence: Script: ex2 h10 p50 s25 -> -0.1831667; s0 -> -0.0523333; s-5 -> -0.001. The intermediates follow from the same inputs: housing factor (10.75 − 50) × 0.1 = −3.925, and size factor (1 − 50/120) × 0.8 + 0.2 = 0.667, whose products match the script output.

accuracy_findings.claim: In the system view, the {ui:galaxy.system.population.workforce} header labels today's growth with one of six words
accuracy_findings.evidence: Population.vue:9-13 renders the header strong label 'Population' (game.json:498) followed by growth_adj '{adj} Growth' using growthToLabel(). There are six labels at Population.vue:112-119: Very High, High, Medium, Low, Zero, Negative (game.json:488-493). A growth <= -1 gets no label (node run: -1.2 -> ""), but growth that negative needs a population of roughly 700 or more above housing, so it can be ignored.

accuracy_findings.claim: {ui:growth_0} (Very High) for the fastest
accuracy_findings.evidence: Population.vue:113 gives boundaries [1, 0.06], and :132 tests growth <= b0 && growth > b1. Node run of the verbatim logic: 0.07 -> 'Very High', 0.06 -> 'High'.

accuracy_findings.claim: {ui:growth_5} (Negative) when population is shrinking
accuracy_findings.evidence: Node run of Population.vue:112-137 verbatim (tmp/help-review/population-acc-r2-label.js): -0.0000164 -> 'Zero', -0.0005 -> 'Zero', -0.001 -> 'Negative', -0.183 -> 'Negative'. growth_4 covers (-0.001, 0.001]. A slowly shrinking system reads 'Zero', and the script confirms this happens in play: h20 p21 at stability 0 has growth -0.00043, which labels 'Zero'.
accuracy_findings.fix: '{ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_5} when population shrinks by 0.001 or more per day; a slower change either way shows {ui:galaxy.system.population.growth_4}.' Add Population.vue:130-137 to sources (see the sources finding).

accuracy_findings.claim: The bar below it fills toward the next whole population point.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Population.vue:19-24: progress-value current = population.value − trunc(population.value), total = 1, increase = population.change. When population is shrinking the same bar drains instead of filling. That is not stated, but it is not contradicted either.

accuracy_findings.claim: sources: Population.vue:110-130
accuracy_findings.evidence: The growth table is at Population.vue:112-119, but growthToLabel(), which does the labeling the page describes, is at :130-137. The listed range stops at 130, the method's first line.

Each range was read and points at the behavior it backs: update_population and population_next_tick, open_system, neutral opening in new/…, claim/4, update_population_class, collect_initial_bonuses, and the header plus progress bar.

accuracy_findings.claim: (missing) Population also drops when a Navarch pillages the system

votes.accuracy_reason: Spot-checked all four accuracy-critic findings in code (stellar_system.ex:1825-1828, constant-fast.ex:10, Population.vue:109-137, raid/3 at stellar_system.ex:297-315) and all hold up: the defense bullet is misleading at fast speed (system_base_defense=0.0 there), growth_5 overclaims (a slowly-shrinking system like -0.0005/day actually shows growth_4 "Zero" per the Population.vue boundary table, not growth_5), the cited source range (110-130) stops right before growthToLabel's body (130-137) which is what the page describes, and the page omits that a pillage/raid also instantly cuts population (raid/3) despite implying daily growth is the only thing that changes it — the growth-label mismatch and the missing pillage effect would actively mislead a new player about a UI element and a mechanic they'll encounter.
votes.clarity_reason: Confirmed the prose runs ~254 words (over the ~250 cap per an awk word-count), "housing factor"/"size factor" are reused in later prose with no plain-English gloss beyond the algebra, and the closing sentence names only 2 of the 6 growth-label words — real first-read friction, though the fast-decline word-count finding is partly overstated since stability -5 does get an implicit worked value; a careful single read still gets the mechanic right, just with avoidable snags.
